Full validated completion/hash acceptance is journaled/fsynced before setting accepted completion state and before journaling/publishing exit grant. findings.status: blocks exact current real runtime plan release
findings.title: Do not signal a completed VM leader solely because its numeric group remains
findings.finding: Normal phase code calls child.wait at line282 before finally invoking reap. reap then probes numeric PGID and can send TERM and later KILL without first checking that the direct VM child is still running or preserving a proven live leader identity. This is conditional on group existence, not literal unconditional signaling, but it still permits forced group signals after normal direct-child completion. It is therefore not a clean normal-exit observe/reap path and can act on a leader-lost numeric group. No claim is made that this would reproduce the separate Swift EPERM observation.
findings.requested_change: Split clean completion/reaping from timeout/error retirement. For an already completed/reaped direct child, observe exact group absence and fail/preserve scratch if unresolved; do not TERM/KILL solely by saved PGID. Signal only while a retained live owned leader identity still authorizes it, rechecking before escalation, and retain uncertainty/errors. Add a focused clean-completion control that records no termination signal plus a still-running timeout path that confirms owned cleanup.

normal_exit_cleanup_review.control_direct_wrapper_fallback: custody-controls.py279-288 sends terminate/kill only if child.poll() is None; completed direct children are not unconditionally signaled. It then samples exact group absence and records an error if unresolved.
normal_exit_cleanup_review.registered_wrapper_groups: custody.py.inspect returns before signaling for terminal absence or sticky identity loss and requires current exact PID/PGID/SID; drain signals only when inspect authorizes. A released but still-live wrapper can be retired under current custody; absent or lost identity is not re-armed.
